case_study_packaging.headline: Women’s health provider captures $716K in annual savings within 10-month sourcing program, realizing 3.2x ROI on consulting fees
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Advantia Health, a fast-growing women’s health platform backed by BlueMountain Capital, had expanded to more than 60 clinics but was still purchasing supplies and services in a highly decentralized manner. Disparate AP systems, fragmented vendor relationships, and limited procurement resources left nearly $19 million in spend unmanaged—constraining margins and private-equity value-creation goals. The leadership team sought a partner that could quickly uncover and lock in material cost reductions while establishing repeatable sourcing discipline.

approach_summary: Completed a data-driven spend analysis across 10 clinical and back-office categories representing $18.9M in annual spend to pinpoint high-value opportunities.
Renegotiated the incumbent Athenahealth revenue-cycle contract, securing a 9% fee reduction and $259K in annual savings without system disruption.
Ran competitive RFPs that consolidated medical-supply distribution to McKesson and optimized lab-services pricing with LabCorp, delivering a combined $197K in savings.
Implemented quick-win clinical initiatives—standardizing IUD order quantities and enrolling in Bayer’s replacement program—to capture $77K in savings within 45 days of project launch.
Developed and executed a make-versus-buy strategy that transitioned sonography staffing in-house, cutting costs by $152K while maintaining coverage across all clinics.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya unlocked $716,000 in verified annual run-rate savings—exceeding the engagement’s minimum savings guarantee by 59% and generating more than 3.2× return on the fixed $225K fee. Beyond hard dollars, the client now benefits from standardized sourcing processes, centralized visibility into spend, and category playbooks that will support future acquisitions and scale.
